subject: LoL carve-outs vs. termination credits — MSA redline (Acme)
messages:
From: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme.com, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-07-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme MSA - redlines on LoL and termination

Hi Laura,

We reviewed the MSA and attached a redline. Two items the business flagged as blockers:

1) Limitation of Liability — your current LoL is capped at the greater of $500k or 3x fees. We need to understand carve-outs: are confidentiality breaches, IP infringement indemnity, and gross negligence excluded from that cap? Our team wants explicit carve-outs for confidentiality and IP.

2) Termination + Prepaid fees — we prepaid an annual amount in the order form. The redline proposes a pro rata refund upon termination for convenience plus 30 days of wind-down assistance. However, the LoL cap appears to limit recovery for termination-related refunds/assist costs. Please confirm whether termination/refund claims would be subject to the LoL.

Attached: Acme_MSA_redline_20260703.docx, Termination_Schedule_ACME_20260703.pdf

Can your legal team propose a short set of compromise sentences we can show our CFO/legal? Happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
John
Procurement
Acme Corp
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: john.smith@acme.com
Date: 2026-07-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme MSA - redlines on LoL and termination

Looping in Rishi (Legal) and Neha (Account Lead). See Acme's redline — two asks that look like classic interplay between LoL carve-outs and termination economics.

Quick thoughts: I think we can:
- Keep standard LoL cap (3x fees) but add explicit carve-outs for confidentiality breach, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity.
- Exclude refunds of prepaid fees and reasonable wind-down assistance from the LoL (or create a separate "termination recovery" cap equal to prepaid fees plus wind-down cap).

Rishi — can you draft 2 short alternatives to present: (A) carve-out language that treats termination refunds and wind-down as carved out (i.e., not subject to LoL), (B) a compromise where termination refunds are subject to a separate, higher cap (e.g., equal to prepaid fees + $50k) but confidentiality/IP remain unlimited.

Neha — heads up: Acme expects pro rata refund + 30d assistance per their order form. If we push back, they'll escalate to finance/CFO.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: john.smith@acme.com
Date: 2026-07-03T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme MSA - redlines on LoL and termination

Laura / Neha — thanks for the heads up and the redline. Drafting two compact alternatives below. I think we should lead with option B in the commercial thread (gives customer predictability without exposing us to open-ended termination refunds).

Option A (customer-friendly):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, termination by Customer for convenience entitles Customer to a pro rata refund of prepaid fees for the unused portion of the applicable Order Form; in addition, Customer shall be entitled to up to thirty (30) days of standard wind-down assistance. Refunds and wind-down assistance shall not be subject to the Limitation of Liability set forth in Section X."

Option B (compromise):
"Except for liability arising from willful misconduct, confidentiality breaches, and indemnities for intellectual property infringement (which shall remain uncapped), liability arising from termination for convenience (including refunds of prepaid fees and reasonable wind-down assistance) shall be subject to a dedicated termination cap equal to the lesser of (i) the total prepaid fees for the affected Order Form and (ii) USD 250,000."

Rationale: Option B keeps confidentiality/IP uncapped, prevents an outsized refund exposure while offering a clean commercial cap. If Acme insists on full carve-out, we should reserve that for Executive approval (finance sign-off).

Action: Laura — propose B to Procurement, indicate willingness to consider A with Exec consent. If they push for A, loop Sales leadership and Finance for approval.

Rishi
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme.com, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-07-04T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MSA - redlines on LoL and termination

Laura — thanks for the quick response and for Rishi's alternatives. Two follow-ups from our side:

1) The CFO will only accept a carve-out for confidentiality and IP if we have an explicit refund path for the prepaid annual fees. They view pro rata refund + wind-down assistance as part of ordinary commercial remedy, not punitive damages.

2) If you propose Option B, they'll want the termination cap to be at least equal to prepaid fees (not the lesser of prepaid and USD 250k).

Can you return with a final position? If you need Exec approval we can schedule a call — our legal/CFO are available Thurs afternoon.

Regards,
John
Procurement
Acme Corp
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: john.smith@acme.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-04T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MSA - redlines on LoL and termination

John — appreciate the clarity. Quick internal note before we propose: Rishi flagged that completely uncapped termination refunds expose us to situations where prepayments for multi-year deals exceed reasonable limits (e.g., refunds + wind-down costs > modelled damages). We are willing to accept that refunds of prepaid fees and wind-down assistance are not swept into the general LoL, provided we add a narrowly tailored protection: refunds equal to pro rata prepaid fees for the *affected* Order Form, and wind-down assistance limited to reasonable documented costs for up to 30 days.

Proposed language (to present to Acme):
"Notwithstanding the Limitation of Liability, Customer shall be entitled to a pro rata refund of prepaid fees paid under the affected Order Form, together with reasonable, documented wind-down assistance fees for up to thirty (30) days. Such refunds and wind-down assistance shall be limited to amounts paid under the affected Order Form and reasonable documented costs; they shall not expand liability for other claims. Confidentiality breaches, willful misconduct and IP indemnities shall remain outside the Limitation of Liability.

This preserves your commercial refund, while keeping open-ended exposure constrained to monies actually paid for that particular Order Form"

Would that work for Acme CFO/legal? If yes, can we get confirmation and I'll mark internal approvals. If they still insist on a broader carve-out without the ‘‘limited to amounts paid under the affected Order Form’’ qualifier, we'll need Exec/Finance sign-off.

Thanks,
Laura
From: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, legal@acme.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-07-05T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MSA - redlines on LoL and termination

Laura / Rishi — that language is close. Our CFO asked for one tweak: instead of "limited to amounts paid under the affected Order Form," they'd prefer the cap be expressed as "the total prepaid fees paid by Customer for the affected Order Form." Functionally the same but clearer for finance. They also asked for an express example in a schedule to avoid ambiguity on multi-year prepayments and whether credits or discounts are included.

Next steps:
- We will accept your proposed carve-out with the tweak to mirror "total prepaid fees" language and an agreed schedule entry showing a sample calculation.
- Please confirm and we'll route the updated doc to Legal for signature.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

John
Procurement
Acme Corp
